newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court orders release of Bhutto's husband.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court orders release of Bhutto's husband.

text.p: A Pakistani court on Wednesday ordered the release of Asif Ali Zardari, husband of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, after it ruled his detention void, Pakistan People's Party leaders said.
A spokesman for Bhutto's party said a two-judge Division Bench of the Sindh High Court in Karachi had declared Zardari's detention void and ordered his release.
Two of Zardari's lawyers took the court order to the Landhi Jail, on the outskirts of Karachi, where he was being held.
The court passed the order on a constitutional petition filed by Zardari's sister, Faryal Talpur, a court official said.
President Farooq Lehari sacked Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Her husband was detained soon after in the city of Lahore under the catch-all Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance and later transferred to Karachi.
Bhutto and Zardari have been at the centre of corruption allegations associated with the former government. Both deny any wrongdoing.
